newsitem.title: USA: CFTC report signals rise is ahead for crude prices.
newsitem.headline: CFTC report signals rise is ahead for crude prices.

text.p: The latest Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Commitment of Traders report disclosed a healthy jump in short positions by funds and local players in NYMEX crude, signalling prices gains ahead on what is expected to be significant short covering, traders said.

"The report shows a fairly hefty increase in short positions among non-commercials. If we get some upside, there could be some significant momentum behind it from short covering," said Tom Bentz, trader with High Yield Analytics in New York.
The CFTC report for the two weeks ended June 17 said short positions by non-commercial players in crude oil rose by 11,761 to 34,625 while long positions dropped by 2,625 to 10,943.

A month ago, dealers said funds had accumulated a large amount of long positions in NYMEX crude that set up the potential for deep sell-offs through heavy long liquidation and made the market vulnerable. Indeed, long liquidation led to spot crude falling more than 15 percent in the past month to 16-month lows.

The CFTC report said commercials decreased their short positions in crude by 8,637 to 242,534. However, total positions of commercial and non-commercials showed a net increase in short positions of 1,987.
"There is definitely a large net short speculative side to this market which could make the market jittery," said Al Lindseth, manager of oil and gas hedge programs at GSC Energy in Atlanta.
